bug_semantics: Bagisto downloadable-product URL delivery uses PHP copy() on an admin-controlled URL. A user who can create or edit a downloadable product sets the link (or sample) type to URL pointing at an internal or non-http target (loopback, link-local/metadata, RFC1918, file://). When a shopper hits ProductController::downloadSample (type=link) or a purchaser hits DownloadableProductController::download, the server copies that URL into a temp file and returns it, producing SSRF (and local-file read via fopen wrappers). CVE-2026-6744 targets the remaining unvalidated copy() in the purchased Downloadable Link Handler at <=2.3.15; sample downloads had already gained a DNS/private-IP check in PR #11069.
flaw_origin: On 2019-06-28, jitendra@webkul.com commit 55b71e1e663c09dd5411ead3664031a2060637d8 ('updated') first added downloadable products and wrote unvalidated copy() of user-supplied URLs in new DownloadableProductController::download (copy($downloadableLinkPurchased->url)) and ProductController::downloadSample (copy of sample_url / sample url). The parent tree has no URL copy sink. Those copy() lines survived moves into Customer/Account/ and are the mechanism CVE-2026-6744 exploits.

reasoning: CVE-2026-6744 is a published (not withdrawn/rejected) CWE-918 in Bagisto's Downloadable Link Handler copy() path. At the stated ceiling v2.3.15 the purchased-link downloader still blindly PHP-copy()s the stored URL, so an admin/catalog user who sets a downloadable link type=URL to an internal target (or file://) makes the shop server fetch it when the customer downloads. Sample downloads were separately guarded in PR #11069 / 9a9606e6ab (v2.3.10+), which is why 2.3.15 ProductController already has validateExternalUrl while DownloadableProductController does not; that matches the vendor note that a remaining issue would be fixed in upcoming releases. The smallest first-write of the unvalidated copy() mechanism is 55b71e1e663c09dd5411ead3664031a2060637d8 (2019-06-28): it added DownloadableProductController and downloadSample copy() sinks. Immediate parent 1700bf1aa231cf37bce3526628e5c38238881c31 lacks the controller and any URL copy(); later path moves (DownloadableProductController → Customer/ → Customer/Account/) are not BICs. The commit is a single-parent non-merge with no reconstructable public members. The post-disclosure fix is 90a962fe20441bb0e0f9c9989de5f600f82a640e (2026-04-22, one day after the CVE), which applies the same SSRF guard to the purchased-link copy() and ships in v2.3.18 / v2.4.3. AI is judged only from the BIC commit object: human Webkul author/committer jitendra@webkul.com, no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot markers, so NOT_AI. GHSA/Snyk still listing no patched version reflects the unlabelled mixed feature commit and a Snyk pointer at the already-guarded sample copy() line, not a missing code change.
